I could not identify the change that fixed TRUNK-6796. The ticket key does not appear in any indexed content I searched, and I had no commit-history tool, so I could not find the commit or PR.

What the current code shows: `computeHashValue()` null-checks both `getPriorDateOfBirth()` and `getPriorDateOfDeath()` before calling `toString()` (lines 444-445). So the null-dereference described in the ticket is guarded in the current version. A regression test, `computeHashValue_shouldNotThrowExceptionWhenPriorDateOfDeathIsNull`, sets only a prior date of birth and asserts no exception, which matches the reported scenario. I did not see the pre-fix code, so I cannot confirm which field was wrongly checked before.

Evidence, best first:

1. openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogData.java:442-447 — the prior-field hashing, including the null-guarded `priorDateOfDeath` at line 445
2. openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogData.java:392-448 — the full `computeHashValue()` method
3. openmrs-core/api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogDataTest.java:18-26 — regression test for a null prior date of death
4. openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/person/PersonMergeLogData.java:363-365 — `getPriorDateOfDeath()` accessor
5. openmrs-core/api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/PersonServiceTest.java:1508-1516 — round-trip test checking the hash is stable after save and reload
